text.p: Italian club Fiorentina said on Friday they had signed Brazilian striker Edmundo to form the world's most potent striker force alongside Argentine Gabriel Batistuta.
"We have hired the Brazilian international centre-foward Edmundo, a player of crystalline class and a lion-like temper," Fiorentina chairman Vittorio Cecchi Gori told reporters.
"They say he's imaginative and unpredictable and that's what soccer is all about. He and Batistuta together, in the future, could give life to the strongest attack in the world."

Italian news agencies said Fiorentina paid 8.0 billion lire ($4.7 million) for the mercurial Edmundo, adding he had signed a four-year contract but would arrive in Italy only in December after completing his duties with Brazilian club Vasco da Gama.
Meanwhile, Batistuta was reported on Friday to have said he would return from holiday in Buenos Aires a few days after Fiorentina begin their pre-season training on Sunday.
Batistuta is reported to be sick and unhappy because of uncertainty over his future.
He has been linked with Spain's Real Madrid and Barcelona, who have baulked at Fiorentina's $23.8 million price tag.
Cecchi Gori played down reports of a row with Batistuta, Italy's top scorer in the 1995-96 season, and appeared to confirm that the player would remain in Florence.
"As far as the Argentine champion is concerned, I know he has asked to return a few days late. That's not a problem," the media mogul said.
"My comfort and that of Fiorentina's fans comes from the fact that, to the champions we already have, we have added even more."
